focus: 'must've' /mʌstəv/ · 'might've' /maɪtəv/ · "can't have" /kɑːntəv/ · 'couldn't have' · certainty-level intonation (confident fall vs uncertain rise-fall)
focus_ar: 'must've' و'might've' و"can't have" و'couldn't have'، ونبرة درجة اليقين (هبوط واثق مقابل تردّد)
arabic_challenge: Past deduction reuses the /əv/ compression from week 5 but for a different purpose: guessing about the past rather than regretting it. The certainty level lives almost entirely in INTONATION — 'must've' falls confidently, 'might've' hedges. Arabic learners produce the right words with the wrong confidence.

isolation.instructions: 'must have' = /mʌstəv/, one unit, meaning 'I'm sure that's what happened'. Say it with a firm FALLING tone: 'He must've forGOTten ↘'. Confidence is in the fall.
isolation.instructions_ar: 'must have' = /mʌstəv/ بمعنى 'أنا متأكد أن هذا ما حدث'. قلها بنبرة هابطة حازمة.

daily_drills.record_this: He must've completely forgotten about the meeting this morning. She must've left already, because her coat is gone. That car must've been really expensive when it was new.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'he must've forgotten'. Is it /mʌstəv/ as one unit, with a confident falling tone?

isolation.instructions: For a guess, use /maɪtəv/ and hedge the tone — slightly rising then falling, lighter and less final: 'She might've misSED it ↗↘'. Uncertainty is audible.
isolation.instructions_ar: للتخمين استخدم /maɪtəv/ مع نبرة متردّدة — صاعدة ثم هابطة، أخفّ وأقل حزمًا.

daily_drills.record_this: She might've missed the train, or perhaps she's just running late. Honestly, it could've been a lot worse than it was. He may've simply misunderstood what I meant.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'she might've missed the train'. Does your tone hedge rather than fall firmly?

isolation.instructions: To say something is IMPOSSIBLE, use "can't have" /kɑːntəv/ with a strong emphatic fall: 'She CAN'T've seen me ↘'. Note: not 'mustn't have' — that is a different meaning entirely.
isolation.instructions_ar: للمستحيل استخدم "can't have" /kɑːntəv/ بهبوط قوي. ملاحظة: ليست 'mustn't have' — معناها مختلف تمامًا.

daily_drills.record_this: She can't have seen me, because I was hidden behind the door. They couldn't possibly have finished the whole project already. He can't have meant that seriously — he was obviously joking.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'she can't have seen me'. Is it /kɑːntəv/ with an emphatic fall, and did you avoid 'mustn't have'?

target_sounds: the three certainty levels back to back

isolation.instructions: Drill the full scale on one sentence: 'He must've left ↘ (sure) / He might've left ↗↘ (maybe) / He can't have left ↘! (impossible)'. Only the modal and the tone change.
isolation.instructions_ar: تدرّب على السلّم كاملًا في جملة واحدة: must've (متأكد) / might've (ربما) / can't have (مستحيل).

sentence_practice: It must've been him — I recognised the voice.
It might've been him, but I'm not sure.
It can't have been him; he was abroad.
daily_drills.record_this: It must've been him, because I clearly recognised the voice. It might've been him, but honestly I'm not completely sure. It can't have been him at all; he was abroad that entire week.
daily_drills.self_check: Say all three versions. Does your tone genuinely change from confident to hedged to emphatic?

isolation.instructions: Deduction usually names the evidence, and the clue is stressed too: 'The lights are OFF, so they must've GONE out.' Link the clue and the conclusion with a smooth 'so'.
isolation.instructions_ar: الاستنتاج يذكر الدليل، والدليل منبور أيضًا: 'The lights are OFF, so they must've GONE out.'
practice: the lights are OFF, so they must've GONE

sentence_practice: The lights are off, so they must've gone out.
Her coat's gone, so she must've left.
No wonder he's tired — he must've been working all night.
daily_drills.record_this: All the lights are off, so they must've gone out for the evening. Her coat has gone from the hook, so she must've left already. No wonder he looks exhausted — he must've been working all night.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'the lights are off, so they must've gone out'. Are both the clue and the conclusion stressed, with a light 'so'?

challenge_sentences: It can't have been him; he was abroad.
The lights are off, so they must've gone out.
daily_drills.record_this: He must've completely forgotten about the meeting. She might've missed the train, or perhaps she overslept. It can't have been him; he was abroad all week. All the lights are off, so they must've gone out somewhere.
daily_drills.self_check: Three checks: modal + /əv/ as one unit, tone matching the certainty level, and "can't have" for impossibility.

test_yourself.instructions: Record yourself solving a small mystery out loud, moving between certainty levels. Then listen back and check whether your CONFIDENCE is audible, not just your grammar.
test_yourself.instructions_ar: سجّل نفسك تحلّ لغزًا صغيرًا بصوت عالٍ، متنقلًا بين درجات اليقين، وتأكد أن ثقتك مسموعة لا نحوك فقط.
test_yourself.passage: Something strange happened last night. When I got home, the kitchen window was open and there was water on the floor. At first I thought someone must've broken in, but nothing was missing, so that can't have been it. My flatmate might've left the window open before she went out — she often forgets. But the water is harder to explain. It could've come from the sink, though I'm fairly sure I turned the tap off. It might've rained heavily while we were out; that would explain the water near the window. Actually, thinking about it, the plant on the windowsill has fallen over, so a cat must've climbed in. It can't have been a person, because the gap is far too narrow. My flatmate must've seen the cat before, because she wasn't surprised at all when I told her.

sounds_to_check.'must've' /mʌstəv/ + confident fall: must've broken in, a cat must've climbed in, she must've seen the cat
sounds_to_check.'might've / could've' + hedged tone: might've left the window open, could've come from the sink, it might've rained
sounds_to_check.\"can't have\" /kɑːntəv/ + emphatic fall: that can't have been it, it can't have been a person
sounds_to_check.evidence linking: stressed clue, weak 'so', stressed conclusion (nothing was MISSing, so that CAN'T have been it)

scoring_guide.90_100: Compressed modals plus genuinely different confidence tones. Ready for week 11.
scoring_guide.70_89: Good; occasionally all guesses sound equally certain.
scoring_guide.50_69: 'must of' appears, or every deduction has the same tone. Repeat days 1-4.
scoring_guide.below_50: Redo days 1-5, drilling the three certainty levels with their distinct intonation.

for_arabic_speakers: Same /əv/ compression as week 5, but here it is GUESSING about the past, not regretting it.
must've = I'm sure (firm fall) · might've/could've = maybe (hedged) · can't have = impossible (emphatic fall).
Use "can't have", never 'mustn't have', for 'that's impossible'.
Your certainty must be audible in the tone — the same words with flat delivery lose the whole meaning.
supplementary_notes.recording_requirement: Record the 'record_this' line daily; compare day 7 with day 1.
